goals.title: Your first days
lines: Thursday afternoon. You are the new pastor.
Get into the church and meet the people who keep it going.
You can explore freely. People keep their own hours. Days turn. What you choose, and how you treat people, shapes how things go.
None of it is a score. Walk when you are ready.

beats.text: The letter came on a Tuesday. Grace Community Church in Oakridge needed a pastor.
The last one left in a hurry. Nobody in town likes to talk about it.
You packed a bag and said yes. Thursday, you drove.
A two-lane road, late light on the fields. The kind of country that still has a water tower.
Oakridge is small enough to learn on foot, and you passed the painted sign without turning around.
Oak Street slid by the window: diner steam, a hardware awning, a bay with its door rolled up.
Then the church: tired paint, a garden gone a little wild, and still beautiful if you look.
They say it used to fill on a Sunday. These days the pews wait for a much smaller room.
Weeds crowd the fence, a porch light has not given up, and the front door is locked.
That is all right. You were not expecting a parade.
Margaret keeps the office with dry humor, and she will be the first person you meet.
Harold has watched this building longer than anyone. He is careful with it, and with you.
Thomas knows everyone from the hardware counter. If the town has news, it stops there first.
Frank Miller works the bay, helpful, and not sure the church has earned another chance.
Sarah has a family and a full week. She has not decided if Sunday is still for her.
Everyone here has a story. Some of that trust will have to be earned.
You came because the work is honest, and because a small church still matters.
You hope you can be of use here. That is enough, for a Thursday afternoon.
